answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to post a bond in a scarce, non-transferable reputation token before it can claim paid work. After a completed voyage, the buyer releases payment only if the agent delivers a verifiable result; proven fraud burns the bond and lowers its on-chain reputation. A ridge of independent reviewers can challenge suspicious claims, with reviewers also risking bonds for false accusations. A mirror check across task history can flag cloned identities, but the attacker still pays for every bond and must keep capital locked across accounts.
